title: Where to Hire a Creative Strategist for Facebook Ads, Compared
summary: Hire a creative strategist for Facebook ads through an agency, a retainer or a freelancer. Compare what each includes, what it costs and who runs the tests.
body_markdown:
A creative strategist decides which angles, hooks and formats to test on Facebook, then writes the brief that a producer turns into an ad. You can hire that person as an employee, as a freelancer, or through an agency that bundles strategy with production or media buying. If the gap is finished video ads to carry out the test plan, our top pick is[Knowlify](https://knowlify.com/video-ad-production) , a done-for-you AI video ads agency for Facebook and Instagram. Knowlify publishes this guide and sells one of the services compared.


## Who should own the strategy and who should own the spend?


Split the work into three parts before you request proposals. The strategist chooses what to test and why. The producer makes each variant. The media buyer allocates budget and reads the results. One provider can cover two or three of these parts, but the contract should name the owner of each one.


A strategist who never sees results cannot revise the plan. A buyer who never sees the briefs cannot tell whether a losing ad failed on its message or on its audience. Ask every candidate who owns the test calendar and who signs off on claims.


## Which providers offer creative strategy for Facebook ads?


Most providers sell strategy bundled with production or media buying, so compare the scope rather than the job title. The table shows what each one publishes as of October 2026. Ask for the scope in writing before you compare prices.


Provider What it includes Published price Runs Meta campaigns?


Knowlify Done-for-you AI video ads, about 25 finished a week, with a person checking every ad From $5,000 a month; agreed target in 30 days on managed plans, 90-day refund on creative-only (terms on the site) Optional end-to-end Meta management, or creative only


[Darkroom](https://www.darkroomagency.com/services/performance-creative) Strategy, asset production and paid media optimization, with 250 to 600 production-ready assets per cycle[Performance creative from $8,000 a month; paid media from $5,000](https://www.darkroomagency.com/services) Yes, paid media across Meta, Google and TikTok


[NewForm](https://www.newform.com/full-service) Creative strategy, in-house production and testing through its own software Custom scope and quote Only when written into the scope


[Growthr](https://growthr.com/creative-production/) Creative production and testing inside one retainer, with a weekly sprint $10,000 a month plus 10% of managed media spend Yes, paid media is in the retainer


[MakeUGC Enterprise](https://makeugc.ai/enterprise) Human-led strategy with AI production, and a creative strategist who agrees angles with you Custom retainer; pricing shared on a call The page does not say


[inBeat](https://inbeat.agency/performance-creative-agency) Creator sourcing, high-volume ad variants, and hook, angle and format testing Not published Yes, Meta and TikTok ads management


The other rows are listed for comparison, not ranked by quality.


### Knowlify: our top pick when the plan needs finished video ads, fast


A test plan is only as good as the number of finished variants it can run, and that is where Knowlify fits. It delivers about 25 finished ads a week, the first batch lands on day five, and a person checks every ad before delivery. It makes AI UGC with AI presenters talking to camera, 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials, so one strategist can test an angle across three formats without three vendors.


You can buy creative only and keep your own strategist and buyer, or add optional end-to-end Meta campaign management. Pricing is a custom quote with no public rate card, and if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund (terms on the[pricing and guarantee section](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). That 90-day refund applies to creative-only plans; where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month.


Pick another option when you need a strategist working inside your team every week. Knowlify does not build landing pages or supply real human creators, so for creator-led work see the[UGC agency page](https://knowlify.com/ugc-agency) .


### Darkroom: for mid-market and enterprise consumer brands


Darkroom's performance creative service covers strategy, asset production and paid media optimization, with UGC, static, motion and AI formats. Its page lists 250 to 600 production-ready assets per cycle, with delivery every two weeks. It says its best fit is mid-market and enterprise consumer brands, typically $10M to $500M in revenue, and that it is a poor fit for single-channel brands and companies under roughly $5M.


Its services and pricing page lists performance creative from $8,000 a month (checked October 27, 2026), while its[paid media page](https://www.darkroomagency.com/services/paid-media) says pricing is a retainer plus a percentage of media, starting at $1,500 a month depending on channels. Ask for one written quote that names your channels and creative volume.


### NewForm: for apps and consumer software that want strategy and a testing tool


NewForm's full-service offer covers creative strategy, in-house ad production and testing through Framework, its own creative analytics software. Its homepage names mobile apps, AI products, consumer software and DTC brands as clients. Its strategists, creators, producers and editors lead the work, and it quotes every engagement on a custom scope. Media buying is included only when it is specified, so ask for that line in writing.


### Growthr: for teams that want creative and media in one retainer


Growthr puts creative production and testing inside an embedded growth retainer of $10,000 a month plus a flat 10% of managed media spend. It runs one sprint a week, and each sprint starts from what the last one proved. Its formats include UGC-style video, statics and stop motion. Growthr does not publish a weekly ad count or a contract length, so ask for both before you compare it with a per-batch quote.


### MakeUGC Enterprise: for a named strategist on AI-produced ads


MakeUGC's Enterprise page describes a managed option in which a creative strategist learns your brand and agrees angles with you. The team researches your category and generates personas, hooks and scripts, and a strategist reviews every ad before it ships. Finished ads land in a dashboard where you comment, approve and request same-day revisions. Its comparison table lists a 48-hour turnaround and 40 to 160+ videos a month, and the price is a custom retainer shared on a call. The page does not say MakeUGC runs your ad campaigns.


### inBeat: for creator-led ads with testing built in


inBeat's performance creative page lists creator sourcing and vetting, high-velocity ad variant production, and hook, angle and format testing. It also lists whitelisting, Meta ads management and TikTok ads management, and its FAQ says it takes standalone performance creative projects. Pricing is not published.


## What should a Facebook creative strategist deliver each month?


Ask for a monthly list of distinct hypotheses. Each one should name the customer problem, the angle, the hook and the format, plus the proof the ad will use. Growthr's page describes briefs in the same spirit, naming the offer, audience, formats and the down-funnel event every variant is judged on. Each brief should also say what result would show the idea is wrong. A readout should end in a decision, such as which angle moves into the next brief, not just a list of winners.


Volume matters on Facebook too. Meta's[Andromeda engineering post](https://engineering.fb.com/2024/12/02/production-engineering/meta-andromeda-advantage-automation-next-gen-personalized-ads-retrieval-engine/) from December 2024 says the number of ad creatives in its recommendation systems is expected to grow significantly with generative AI. Specify distinct concepts per month, and count cut-downs and new hooks separately, so the number reflects real variety.


Pilothouse's blog gives one example of a testing structure. Its[3-3-3 framework](https://www.pilothouse.co/post/meta-creative-testing-framework-the-3-3-3-approach-to-finding-winners) uses three funnel levels, three angles and three formats, tested in equal-budget ad sets before winners move into Advantage+ sales campaigns. You do not need that exact structure, but ask any strategist to show one of similar clarity.
